summary: DEF-015 containment for one function. Revokes EXECUTE on public.el_signature_progress(uuid) from PUBLIC and anon, and grants it explicitly to authenticated and service_role. Grants only — no function body, signature, table, policy or trigger is altered.

problem.context: The launch-readiness audit (docs/audits/2026-07-27-launch-readiness-e2e.md, DEF-015) enumerated 93 SECURITY DEFINER functions that anon may execute and that contain no internal authorisation check. public.el_signature_progress is on that list, in risk class 1 — data disclosure on a caller-supplied UUID.
problem.cause: Introduced by 20260727140000 as SECURITY DEFINER without revoking the default PUBLIC EXECUTE grant Postgres applies to every new function. It is an internal helper — the single implementation of the engagement-letter signing rule — and was never intended as a public endpoint.
problem.exposure: To an unauthenticated caller holding an engagement-letter UUID it discloses the signing rule and the required/signed signatory counts. Modest in isolation, but it is an oracle on an enumerable identifier with no token check.
problem.deliberately_out_of_scope: public_get_engagement_letter_for_signing and public_sign_engagement_letter_as_signatory KEEP their anon grants. A client following an emailed signing link has no session; both authorise on the signing token itself, matching the public_get_onboarding pattern. Revoking those would break the client-facing signing journey.
problem.scale: This is 1 of the 93 functions in DEF-015. It is authored separately because it is a defect introduced by this repo yesterday, is unambiguous, and needs no product decision. The remaining 92 require the batched, risk-classed review described in docs/audits/2026-07-28-remediation-plan.md.

expected_objects.object: anon can no longer EXECUTE public.el_signature_progress(uuid); authenticated and service_role can
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_grants / has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.el_signature_progress(uuid)', 'EXECUTE') -> false; same check for 'authenticated' -> true. Then call the function with the anon key and expect a permission-denied error rather than a result.

expected_objects.object: The client-facing signing journey still works end to end
expected_objects.verify_via: With the anon key and no session, call public_get_engagement_letter_for_signing with a valid signatory token — it must still return the letter and its progress block. That function is SECURITY DEFINER and reaches el_signature_progress as the definer, so the revoke must not affect it. This is the regression that would matter.
expected_objects.evidence: Callers are SECURITY DEFINER and reach el_signature_progress as the definer; grants-only migration cannot affect them. No body/signature change.

expected_objects.object: lifecycle_onboarding_gates still evaluates the signature rule
expected_objects.verify_via: db_rpc lifecycle_onboarding_gates for an application with signatory rows and confirm engagement_letter_signed and activation_ready are computed as before. It is SECURITY DEFINER and calls the helper as the definer.
expected_objects.evidence: Callers are SECURITY DEFINER and reach el_signature_progress as the definer; grants-only migration cannot affect them. No body/signature change.

rollback.assessment: Trivial: GRANT EXECUTE ... TO anon restores the previous state. Doing so reinstates the DEF-015 exposure.
rollback.data_risk: None. Grants only; no data is read or written by the migration.

steps: Apply 20260728120000_revoke_anon_el_signature_progress.sql via the Lovable migration flow.
Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).
Immediately exercise the client signing link end to end — this is the one thing a bad revoke would break.
After apply: refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version.
Notify Claude to run the expected-object verification and complete this receipt (move out of pending/).

post_apply_followups: 92 functions remain on the DEF-015 list. They need enumeration with signature, owner, security mode, grants and intended caller, then revoke-by-default and regrant-by-exception, batched by risk class so a mistaken revoke cannot take out the client-facing token-gated endpoints in one go.

A CI check should fail when a new SECURITY DEFINER function is created without an explicit grant decision. Every function in this repo currently inherits PUBLIC EXECUTE silently — which is exactly how this one ended up on the list.
